questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Brunei?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Brunei article.

questions.proof: The capital of Brunei is Bandar Seri Begawan.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Brunei?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Brunei on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Brunei article.

questions.proof: It is located on the northern coast of the island of Borneo and is surrounded on its landward sides by Malaysia.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Brunei?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Brunei article.

questions.proof: Brunei's official language and national language is Malay and English language.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “From the 14th to the 16th centuries Brunei Darussalam was the seat of a powerful sultanate extending over Sabah, Sarawak and the southern _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “southern”. It names more than one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Brunei article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: From the 14th to the 16th centuries Brunei Darussalam was the seat of a powerful sultanate extending over Sabah, Sarawak and the southern Philippines.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In 2011 the IMF said that Brunei was one of two countries (the other being _____) with no public debt.”

hints.nudge: The missing word is a name, not an everyday word. Only one of these names makes the sentence true.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Brunei article, under the heading “Revenue”.

questions.proof: In 2011 the IMF said that Brunei was one of two countries (the other being Libya) with no public debt.
